findings.claim: The Ten Obligatory Acts "include all of the Five Pillars (Salah, Sawm, Zakah, Hajj and Jihad) plus five additional duties"; the inline definition and the glossary repeat that they "include the Five Pillars".
findings.truth: The Ten Obligatory Acts (furu ad-din) are Salah, Sawm, Zakah, Khums, Hajj, jihad, Amr bil ma'ruf, Nahi anil munkar, Tawalla and Tabarra. They hold four of the Five Pillars, not five: the Shahadah is not among them. Jihad is not a Pillar of Sunni Islam.
findings.evidence: spec 3.1.5.2 (Five Pillars of Sunni Islam and the Ten Obligatory Acts of Shi'a Islam); the lesson's own list at n8 gives the correct ten and omits the Shahadah

findings.claim: Revision tip: "The extra 5 include Khums, Jihad, commanding good, forbidding evil, and devotion to the Prophet's family."
findings.truth: Six of the Ten sit outside the Five Pillars: Khums, jihad, Amr bil ma'ruf, Nahi anil munkar, Tawalla and Tabarra.
findings.evidence: recount of the lesson's own list at n8

findings.claim: Surah 112 quoted as "He is Allah, the One, Allah is Eternal and Absolute. None is born of Him, He is unborn. There is none like unto Him."
findings.truth: That wording appears in no standard translation. Abdel Haleem reads: "Say, 'He is God the One, God the eternal. He begot no one nor was He begotten. No one is comparable to Him.'"
findings.evidence: api.quran.com translation 85 (Abdel Haleem), chapter 112, fetched 18 Sep 2026

findings.claim: Q2 is typed "1 mark - Give/Name" but asks for two acts and its scheme awards "1 mark for each, up to 2 marks"; the accepted list also omits jihad.
findings.truth: Each religion is examined by two five-part questions of 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks, so no 2-mark question exists on this paper. Jihad is one of the Ten Obligatory Acts and is not a Pillar, so it must be accepted.

findings.claim: Q4 model answer: "Surah 112 declares Allah is 'One, Eternal and Absolute.'"
findings.truth: Not verbatim in a standard translation. Abdel Haleem gives "He is God the One" and "No one is comparable to Him".

findings.claim: Q5 model answer: "It affirms Tawhid, which the Qur'an calls the most fundamental belief (Surah 112)."
findings.truth: Surah 112 states God's oneness and uniqueness. It makes no ranking claim about which belief is most fundamental, so the attribution is invented.

findings.claim: Qur'an 2:163 quoted as "Your God is one God. There is no deity except Him, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful".
findings.truth: A hybrid: "There is no deity except Him" is Sahih International, while "the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful" is Khattab. Reference and meaning are right, so no marks are at risk.

findings.claim: The Shahadah is given as "La ilaha illa Allah wa-Muhammad rasul Allah" translated "Muhammad is the Prophet of Allah".
findings.truth: Rasul means messenger, and most GCSE texts translate the second clause "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah". Both renderings are accepted in marking, so no marks are at risk, but the English does not match the transliteration printed beside it.

findings.claim: Card 4 front: "5% of savings), _____ (fasting during Ramadan), and Hajj (pilgrimage to Makkah at least once in a lifetime)" with answer "Sawm".
findings.truth: The front is a fragment sliced out of the key-fact box and starts mid-number. A single-word answer needs a question front.

findings.claim: Card 5 answer is "Shirsquoa" and its front is the fragment "The key difference is that _____ Muslims have additional obligations...".
findings.truth: The answer is a mangled HTML entity: Shi’a collapsed to Shirsquoa. It should read Shi'a Muslims, on a proper question front.
findings.evidence: entity corruption visible in the stored value

findings.claim: Q2 is typed "1 mark - Give/Name" but asks for two groups and awards "1 mark for each, up to 2 marks".
findings.truth: The five parts are worth 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks. There is no 2-mark question on this paper.

findings.claim: Hajj "attracts over two million Muslims from around the world each year".
findings.truth: Recorded attendance was 1,845,045 (2023), 1,833,164 (2024) and 1,673,230 (2025). Only 2019 (2,489,406) passed two million. "More than 1.5 million" is safe for every recent year.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Hajj pilgrim table, fetched 18 Sep 2026

findings.claim: Q4 model answer: "Over two million Muslims from every nation stand together at Arafat".
findings.truth: Same stale figure as F12; the model answer must match the corrected text.

findings.claim: Q2 is typed "1 mark - Give/Name" but asks for two rituals and awards "1 mark for each, up to 2 marks".
findings.truth: The five parts are worth 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks. There is no 2-mark question on this paper.

findings.claim: Card 4 answer is "Shirsquoa" on the fragment front "_____ Muslims pay 20% of their surplus income..."; card 5 answers "Muslims" on the fragment "5% of savings) is paid by all _____ while Khums (20% of surplus income) is an additional duty for Shi'a Muslims".
findings.truth: Card 4 carries the same collapsed entity as lesson 1. Card 5's answer word sits inside its own front, so the card answers itself; both fronts start mid-sentence.

findings.claim: At Mina "pilgrims throw pebbles at three stone pillars".
findings.truth: The three pillars were replaced by long walls (the Jamarat) after 2004 to reduce crushing. GCSE textbooks still say pillars and the symbolism is unchanged, so no marks are at risk.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Stoning of the Devil / Jamarat Bridge

findings.claim: "The Ka'aba is believed to be directly below God's throne in heaven."
findings.truth: Muslim tradition places al-Bayt al-Ma'mur, or the Gate of Heaven, directly above the Ka'aba rather than the Throne itself. The sentence is framed as a belief and nothing in the spec turns on it.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Kaaba (axis mundi, Gate of Heaven above it)

findings.claim: "Examiners specifically look for the conditions that must be met before lesser jihad can be declared".
findings.truth: A fabricated examiner claim. The instruction to learn three conditions with Qur'anic support stands on its own.
findings.evidence: house rule: no invented examiner or mark-scheme claims

findings.claim: Revision tip on the Ashura key fact ends "Examiners love this contrast."
findings.truth: A second fabricated examiner claim. The advice survives without it.
findings.evidence: house rule: no invented examiner or mark-scheme claims

findings.claim: Q2 is typed "1 mark - Give/Name" but asks for two conditions and awards "1 mark for each, up to 2 marks".
findings.truth: The five parts are worth 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks. There is no 2-mark question on this paper.

findings.claim: Card 5 answers "Lesser" on the front "_____ Jihad - The Physical Struggle Lesser jihad refers to the physical or military struggle to defend Islam when it is under threat".
findings.truth: The answer word is printed inside its own front, so the card gives itself away, and it duplicates card 3 ("lesser jihad"). The front is a heading run into the paragraph below it.

findings.claim: Card 4 answers "Muslim" on the front "It simply means 'struggle' or 'striving' and refers to the effort every _____ must make to follow God's path".
findings.truth: A single-word answer on a fragment front that tests nothing; the lesson's Muharram definition supports a real card instead.

findings.claim: Q4 model answer states "The Prophet Muhammad himself described the inner struggle as the 'greater' jihad" and offers that hadith as the source.
findings.truth: The lesson text itself explains that this hadith is graded weak and is absent from the six authoritative collections. The model answer drops that caveat. The hadith is accepted as a source in marking, so no marks are at risk, but the two passages contradict each other.

findings.claim: Q5 mark scheme carries board level descriptors and the line "Maximum Level 2 if no reference to religion", plus "0 marks: No relevant content."
findings.truth: "Level 2" is a banned band name and the descriptors are pasted mark-scheme wording. The bands must be described in house vocabulary (Top band / Upper-mid band / Lower-mid band / Lower band).
findings.evidence: scripts/_retrofc/CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md banned-string list and copyright distancing rule

findings.claim: Key fact: "The Qur'an teaches that Ibrahim agreed to sacrifice his son even though he was tempted by Shaytan (the devil). At three places, the angel Jibril told Ibrahim to 'Pelt him,' so Ibrahim threw seven pebbles and Shaytan left."
findings.truth: The Qur'an (37:102) carries the dream and the son's assent, but the temptation by Shaytan and the pelting are not in the Qur'an at all; they come from later Muslim tradition. Attributing them to scripture misleads a student who cites them as Qur'anic.

findings.claim: Q4 model answer offers as "Reference to sacred writing" that "the Qur'an teaches that Ibrahim agreed to sacrifice his son even though he was tempted by Shaytan".
findings.truth: Same misattribution as F25; the model answer must match the corrected text.

findings.claim: Q2 reads "Give one ways in which Muslims celebrate Eid al-Fitr."
findings.truth: The question is ungrammatical as printed; it should read "Give one way".
findings.evidence: reading of the stored question text

findings.claim: Q6 model answer cites "'Verily it is only a festival for he whose fast Allah has accepted' - this Hadith".
findings.truth: The saying is not traceable to the six authoritative collections; it is normally reported as a saying of the early Muslims rather than a hadith of the Prophet. sunnah.com blocked automated checking, so the label is unverified rather than proved wrong. Recommend relabelling it a traditional saying, or dropping it, in the next content pass.
findings.evidence: sunnah.com returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch on 18 Sep 2026

findings.claim: Zakat al-Fitr is given as "approximately £2–£5" in the body, the glossary and a model answer.
findings.truth: The duty is one sa' of staple food per person, about 2.6-3 kg, and UK charities reset the cash equivalent every year, so a fixed pound range goes stale. No authoritative current UK figure could be fetched (Islamic Relief returned 403, NZF 404), so the figure is not corrected here.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Zakat al-Fitr (one sa', 2.6-3 kg); UK charity pages unreachable 18 Sep 2026

findings.claim: Two revision tips read "Cover this box. Write down what you recall about qur'an states." and "...about shi'a Muslims."
findings.truth: Auto-generated tips truncated into nonsense. Not a factual error, but they are student-facing and belong in the tip-quality sweep.
findings.evidence: reading of the stored data-revision-tip attributes

findings.claim: Lesson titles do not match lesson content. L1 is titled "The Five Pillars, Shahadah and Salah" but teaches no Salah; L2 is titled "Zakah and Sawm" but teaches Salah and Sawm with no Zakah; L3 is titled "Hajj" but opens with Zakah and Khums; L4 is titled "Jihad" but gives its second half to the three festivals.
findings.truth: The teaching is complete and in spec order when read straight through - Five Pillars, Shahadah, Salah, Sawm, Zakah, Khums, Hajj, jihad, festivals - and every description matches its own lesson. Only the titles are out of step, and a student revising Zakah opens the wrong lesson. Title is not an editable field in this harness, so this needs Tom's call. Recommended retitle, matching the free-tier sibling unit: L1 "The Five Pillars, Ten Obligatory Acts and Shahadah", L2 "Salah and Sawm", L3 "Zakah and Hajj", L4 "Jihad and Islamic Festivals", L5 unchanged.

findings.claim: Lesson 4 teaches Id-ul-Adha, Id-ul-Fitr and Ashura in full, and lesson 5 teaches the same three festivals again at greater length, including a second Karbala account.
findings.truth: The duplication is real but the two passages agree on every fact, and lesson 5 adds Qurbani, Zakat al-Fitr and the Kufa invitation. Either cut the festival half of lesson 4 back to a signpost, or keep the overlap as deliberate revision. Not a factual error, so no edit is written.

findings.claim: Every 4-mark question in the unit is typed "4 marks - Explain Similarities & Differences", including stems that ask for two ways rather than a comparison (L3 Q6, L5 Q3).
findings.truth: The spec fixes the marks and the paper structure but not the stems. Two house labels already exist in this board's corpus for the "Explain two ways in which..." stem, so choosing between them is a corpus-wide call that belongs with the question-type relabel programme.
findings.evidence: spec assessment section lines 1826-1830; label census across scripts/_retrofc/units/religious-studies*

summary: Doctrine is largely sound: the Qur'anic references at 20:14, 5:6, 62:9, 2:185, 97:3, 2:43 and 3:97 all check out, as do the 2.5% zakah rate and the nisab, khums at one fifth, the Hajj sequence and sites, the Sunni and Shi'a prayer counts and Karbala in 680 CE. The costly errors are the claim that the Ten Obligatory Acts hold all Five Pillars (they leave out the Shahadah, and jihad is not a Pillar), a Surah 112 quotation in wording no translation uses, the pelting of Shaytan attributed to the Qur'an, a banned 'Level 2' band name with pasted mark-scheme descriptors in lesson 5, a 2-mark award on all four second-part questions when this paper has none, and six broken or self-answering flashcards, two of them carrying a collapsed HTML entity. The lesson titles are also one step out of line with what each lesson teaches.
